cause: Each repair was verified only in the direction it was written to block. The author tested that a guard refuses, never that it still permits the legitimate case; tested the shape that motivated the bug, never the neighbouring shapes; and tested that a gate exists, never that it can actually fire. Self-review shares the author's blind spots by construction, so a REVISE from W4a is not evidence that independent review is unnecessary - it is evidence the author can find some defects, not the ones rooted in their own model of the problem.
prevention: Two rules. First, every guard gets tests on both sides: the refusal AND the permitted case that proves the guard did not become a no-op, plus the neighbouring shapes of whatever motivated it. The liveness-evidence boundary here is pinned at four points (live, in-grace, at-grace, well-past) precisely so a future tightening cannot silently disable the exit. Second, a repair round is not complete until an independent context-isolated reviewer has challenged it; re-review after every repair, not once at the end. Prove each new test red against the pre-repair tree, because a test written after the fix routinely passes on the broken tree - one here did, and only the independent reviewer noticed.
summary: Closing a 4x-recurring defect took four adversarial review rounds. The original implementation carried one P0 the author's own W4a missed entirely, and then every P1 in rounds 2 and 3 was a defect in a previous repair rather than in the original work: a fix that made adopted claims permanently un-renewable, a fix that closed only the rarest lease shape while leaving the most common one open, and a scope gate that compared a record to itself and could therefore never fire.
title: Test both directions of every guard, and never let the author be the last reviewer
